findings.title: Keyboard cannot move the PAYG slider between plan ticks: every arrow press is snapped straight back
findings.claim: The release guard `if (v <= SM_LAST_TICK) { const s = Math.round(v); slider.value = String(s); ... }` runs on every `change`, and for a range input the browser fires `input` then `change` on each ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/PageUp/PageDown press (keyboard changes are committed immediately, unlike a drag). With `step="0.01"` one press moves v by 0.01, so `Math.round(v)` is always the tick the thumb was already on and the value is written back before a second press can accumulate.
findings.failure_scenario: Slider focused at tick 0 (100 devices). ArrowRight: `input` → v=0.01 → sliderToDevices → 100 (no change), `change` → 0.01 <= 2 → slider.value='0'. Thumb never leaves 0; 500 and 1,000 are unreachable by keyboard from the left. From End (3 → 150,000) ArrowLeft walks the continuous range down to 2 (1,000), then ArrowLeft → 1.99 → snapped back to 2, so Startup (500) and Pilot (100) are unreachable from the right too. Only Home/End and the continuous region respond. Pre-existing (it was worse before this commit, which snapped everywhere), but this commit now owns the snap rule and the keyboard case is where it still misbehaves.
findings.suggested_fix: On `change`, when v is inside the tick region and `Math.round(v)` equals the tick the slider was already on but v itself moved, step to the neighbouring tick in the direction of travel (track the last committed tick); alternatively handle ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/PageUp/PageDown in a `keydown` handler that jumps to the adjacent tick while v <= SM_LAST_TICK and lets the browser's native step apply only past it.

findings.title: `will-change: transform` on four field-sized wrappers blows Firefox's will-change area budget
findings.claim: Firefox caps will-change-promoted area per document at 3x the viewport area (`kWillChangeAreaMultiplier`), measured on the frame's untransformed size. Each `.wave-bg__wave` is 1.98 viewport areas on desktop (110%x180%), so the second wrapper already exceeds the budget; Firefox then ignores the hint for the remaining wrappers and logs 'Will-change memory consumption is too high. Budget limit is the document surface area multiplied by 3...' once per page. The hint buys nothing here: a running transform animation is composited in Chromium, WebKit and Gecko without it, and the animations start at page load.
findings.failure_scenario: Open /pricing/, /, /products/thingsboard-pe/ or /products/paas/ in Firefox with the console open: a will-change budget warning appears on every page using the component. Animation behaviour is unaffected (OMTA does not need will-change), so this is console noise and a misleading hint, not a visual defect.
